[ This is a sealed-bid, second-price auction with independent private values uniformly distributed. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Shading risks losing when winning would be profitable, and overbidding risks negative payoff if the second price exceeds value. With no informative history and only one round, no learning applies. Therefore, bid exactly my value ($32). If tied at the top, the random tie-break is acceptable because expected payoff remains nonnegative when bidding truthfully. ]

Three-bidder, sealed-bid, second-price auction with independent private values. The dominant, profit-maximizing strategy for a risk-neutral bidder is to bid one’s true value, since the price paid is the second-highest bid. There’s no past history to exploit and only 1 round, so no learning adjustments. Tie probability at exactly my value is negligible; shading or overbidding can only reduce expected profit. I will bid my true value of 41 to maximize expected long-run (and current) profit.
